comparison.test_cohort: identical for Regime S and Regime T
comparison.validation_cohort: identical source-normal parent recordings for Regime S and Regime T
comparison.only_intended_difference: Regime T fits on the released target-normal training allocation (RoboticArm 27, BrushlessMotor 18); Regime S reserves exactly that allocation unused
comparison.adaptation_budget: released few-shot allocation only; same-parent siblings are blocked, not trained on

validation.target_adaptation_use: the released adaptation allocation is train-only in Regime T and reserved in Regime S; blocked siblings are used by neither regime for anything

metrics.protocol_a_implementation: strict pairwise normal_score < anomaly_score; ties zero
metrics.protocol_b_implementation: one pinned standard-library implementation for every paired model

score_aggregation.protocol_a: median of window reconstruction errors, exactly as pinned upstream
score_aggregation.provenance: every segment score stores all contributing window_ids

robotic_arm.unit_sampled: parent_recording with all child segments retained
robotic_arm.paired_comparisons: same parent draws for both models; interval on metric difference

brushless_motor.limitation: fault and acquisition-session effects remain non-identifiable

forbidden_units: RoboticArm sibling segments treated as independent

supersedes.scope: training/adaptation role labels only; the Phase-2.1 common evaluation cohort, source-validation cohort, metrics, threshold policy, score aggregation and uncertainty design are carried forward unchanged

primary_scientific_question: Does access to the released few-shot target-normal training allocation improve anomaly detection under domain shift?

definition.target_adaptation_observed: released target-normal training segments actually consumed by Regime T
definition.target_adaptation_parent_groups: distinct physical parent recordings containing those released segments
definition.target_adaptation_blocked_siblings: further normal segments of those same parent recordings; consumed by nothing
definition.target_adaptation_parent_closure: observed + blocked siblings; a leakage bookkeeping total, never a training budget

adaptation_budget.rationale: Parent independence requires sibling segments of an adaptation parent to be excluded from evaluation. It does not require them to become adaptation training data. IMAD-DS intentionally exposes only the released allocation, so the primary Regime-T experiment consumes only that allocation.

blocked_sibling_use.sole_purpose: enforce parent independence of the common evaluation cohort

protocol_roles.source_training: model fitting and learned preprocessing statistics
protocol_roles.source_validation: early stopping, model/window/feature selection, threshold calibration
protocol_roles.target_adaptation: Regime T model fitting; reserved and unused in Regime S
protocol_roles.adaptation_sibling_blocked: nothing; withheld solely to keep adaptation parents out of evaluation
protocol_roles.common_evaluation: final reported metrics only, identical for Regime S and T
protocol_roles.exclusivity: every segment carries exactly one primary protocol role

T-parent-complete.definition: adaptation on all 123 normal RoboticArm segments of the 18 adaptation parents
T-parent-complete.labelling_requirement: must be reported as a larger adaptation-budget experiment and never conflated with the primary few-shot Regime T
